residue.text: Unresolved supplied attribution limit: 60- and 105-second doses leave 60 versus 15 quiet seconds before sampling. Settling, redistribution and sampling disturbance confound agitation-only attribution. Inference: recurrent adversity supports a boundary for these complete protocols; no signal leaves boundaries outside the admissible range unknown. Other materials and scales remain untested.

Supplied alternatives omitted from the six-trial dose schedule remain hypotheses: ATT repeats fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds without optical restart, testing reliable dispensability against exceptional or sampling-mediated success. INV compares enabled optical control with timer-stopped 900 rpm, logging shadow decisions, and compares fixed-duration speeds or matched brief pauses. These require a separate allocation within six trials; they cannot be added to three dose pairs.

Supplied unresolved residue: specks could be bubbles, reflections or undissolved dye; bubble fraction and absolute concentration are unmeasurable. Common-aliquot repeatability is not calibration; rpm is commanded without tachometer verification. Matched 900 rpm final samples and actual rule-driven prolongation are absent. Relative time savings and reliable future success remain unknown.

summary.text: Observed synthetic anchor: one 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and yielded final attenuations 0.204, 0.209, 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This bounded counterexample questions universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm and optical stability. Fluctuating 900 rpm images and specks do not establish sample harm or identify its mechanism; stable images alone cannot establish success.

Hypothesis-testing construction: three fresh-recipe pairs compare preassigned 900 rpm for 60 versus 105 seconds from second zero, exhausting six trials. Use 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye; reverse duration order across pairs, fix addition location, bottle and locked camera, rinse between trials, and alternate sampling order. Sample at second 120, withdrawing 1 mL per depth within ten seconds. Log stops and quiet durations; optical decisions never choose doses.

Proposed adverse detector: recurrent paired 105-second final spread above 4 percent while 60-second spread is at most 4 percent. Report raw readings, durations and every failure; normalize max-minus-min by mean using water/common-aliquot references. Record five-second side spread, depression and speck frames as secondary signals. Optical worsening alone indicates interface cost. Use the spill tray; liquid escape requires immediate cessation.

Hypothesis A: extra agitation worsens the sample proxy; rival B: it preserves or improves it, possibly rescuing short-dose failures. Both targets passing despite worse images supports interface cost without sample harm. INV adds an unobserved return-loop hypothesis: agitation renews disturbances that command more agitation. Fixed doses sever optical control, but this comparison alone cannot establish that loop or distinguish its mechanism.
